title: Chrome browsing history
whyItMatters: Lists every page visited, when, how often and what was typed into the address bar. It reveals health, money, relationship and work interests in detail.
source: Chromium user data directory docs, History lives in each macOS profile: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/user_data_dir.md
notes: One History file per profile. Sibling History-wal and History-journal files are not counted separately; the database is never opened.

cleanup.signOut: In Chrome open Settings > You and Google and choose Turn off, so the Google account keeps its data but stops syncing this Mac.
steps: Close every Chrome window so the history database is not in use.
In Chrome open the history page and clear browsing data for all time.
Delete the History file named in the plan if it is still there; leave the rest of the Chrome folder alone.
cleanup.risk: The list of sites visited on this Mac is gone. Saved passwords and bookmarks in the same profile are not touched.
cleanup.source: Google Chrome Help, Delete browsing data in Chrome: https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95582
